1.1 Central method

      The proposed plan replaces parent-style smooth-max optimization with an exact-objective search built around three mechanisms:

      First, build diverse feasible grids on even-sized grids using quantized integers. The main discrete representation is h_i = q_i / M with integer levels q_i ∈ {0,...,M}, M = 4 for the primary run, and total integer mass exactly sum(q_i) = n*M/2. Every move transfers one unit from one cell to another, preserving total mass by construction, so no artificial repair disturbs the current candidate during the search.

      Second, use exact-score Simulated Descent Move Search (SDMS) on the integer levels. It evaluates every proposed move using the literal returned evaluator: exact np.correlate(h, 1-h, full) * dx, including finite support and all 2n-1 offsets. It never substitutes circular autocorrelation, “1 minus minimum autocorrelation,” or a smoothed minimal scalar surrogate for scoring. Moves are not only random; they are biased by exact local row gradients of the active largest correlations. Earlier simple transport or single-neighbor steepest descent is accelerated through a feasibility-preserving LP fallback for simple ordinary starvation cases.

      Third, use a non-smooth continuous polish stage called PairTransferPolish (PTP). It is structured as an active-gradient direction pool of feasible unit transfers, h_a -= t, h_b += t, evaluated by backtracking (source/sink fixed) to find an actual exact decrease in the true maximum. This is a coordinate-direction descent adapted to the budget hyperplane with pair-bound capacities. If ordinary greedy pair moves are also stalled, the active LP is attempted to give a global linear prediction. There is no penalty-stage or annealing-based optimization of a surrogate objective for accepting the solution.
